principle.original_value: Most or all primary system components are integrated inside the reactor pressure vessel.
principle.assessment: The integral layout places most or all primary components in the vessel. The integral PWR simulator is educational evidence; neither the figure nor simulator proves deployment or completes maturity, strength and challenge review.

strength.assessment: Integral layout reduces external primary piping by locating most or all primary components in the vessel. This configuration benefit is not a guarantee of smaller total plant footprint, lower cost or elimination of every pipe-break scenario.

challenge.original_value: Inspection access and validation of natural-circulation designs
challenge.assessment: Integral-system maintenance and in-service inspection remain challenges; natural-circulation and low-driving-head designs introduce scaling and code-validation uncertainty. Applies to designs using those mechanisms, not an assertion that every integral PWR uses unpumped circulation. The working paper does not qualify any plant. Supports design-specific scaling, experimental validation and weak-driving-force limitations when natural circulation is used. Educational modelling and passive classification do not establish operational plant performance, automatic safety superiority or regulatory qualification. Inspection-access component is supported separately by the NEXSHARE paper.

strength.assessment: Supports the direct-cycle configuration as a design characteristic; it does not establish an economic advantage, universal turbine shielding rule or plant-specific safety assessment.

challenge.original_value: Two-phase stability and radioactive steam circuit

Supports the radioactive primary-steam circuit and shielding implications of water activation, including nitrogen-16. Does not imply current site dose exceedance, arbitrary contamination of the turbine, a mandatory delay-loop design or current regulatory instructions.

principle.original_value: A pulsed discharge forms a transient dense pinched plasma region.
principle.assessment: Annular current-carrying layer between coaxial electrodes moves axially, turns inward at electrode ends and forms compressed hot region. Not pure uniform cylinder or a static confined state. Breakdown, axial acceleration, radial collapse/column/disruption sequence under pulsed high-current drive. Characteristic micro/nanosecond intervals depend on scale; mixed emission processes do not prove a uniform thermal plasma.

strength.assessment: D-D focus produces pulsed neutron radiation as well as beams/X-rays. No claim that neutron yield gives net energy or that all emitted neutrons are thermal. Compact pulsed neutron-source purpose and specific deuterium observations. PF6~1cps/100shot series, component50Hz/lifetime expectations and PF1000 distinct energy regimes are not combined into an imaginary operating point. Source authors report mixed thermal/beam contributions; no net-power qualification.

challenge.original_value: Repeatable neutron output, driver-to-radiation efficiency and electrode heat loads
challenge.assessment: Reliable repeatable radiation and energy transfer/generation efficiency are device/application challenges; certain improved devices already achieve reproducible output. Efficiency means input-to-useful-radiation transfer, not net fusion energy or electrical conversion. Per-shot input energy heats electrodes and cooling matters for repetition. The measured7kJ setup shows heat load can persist even for poor/no pinch and need not track neutron yield. Local voltage/pressure fit is not universal all-DPF heat fraction or an energy-producing reactor.

TRIM stopping and assumed target composition are models; these device examples do not define a universal efficiency or establish energy production.

principle.original_value: Reports attribute anomalous heat or nuclear products to electrochemically loaded palladium.
principle.assessment: Reports the attribution of claimed excess heat/nuclear products to a loaded palladium cathode. Conventional fusion-product yields were insufficient for the claimed heat; the attribution is a claim, not confirmed spontaneous lattice fusion. Defines the tested hypothesis of nuclear coalescence in highly loaded Pd during electrolysis and its isotope/material controls. The summary's erroneous 1995 announcement date is not adopted. Neither that hypothesis nor reported heat is accepted as demonstrated nuclear fusion.

strength.assessment: Supports empirical testability through closed-system calorimetry, total gas recombination, alternative methods and simultaneous commensurate nuclear-product measurements. This is a methodological strength of a falsifiable claim, not an achieved positive nuclear result. PDF15 is browser page 4 of 5 of the retained NCAS edition, not an invented government printed page. Actual material/isotope controls and closed calorimeters illustrate testing of the heat hypothesis. Instrument sensitivity, calibration, isotope purity and loading diagnostics limit the assessment; testability is not useful power production.

challenge.original_value: Replication failures and inconsistent product accounting
challenge.assessment: The 1989 panel records inconsistent replication and a mismatch between reported heat and known fusion products. It explicitly cannot categorically prove or disprove all claims. The retained 1999 NCAS Internet edition has 2006 browser footers; no original retrieval date or current universal result is inferred. The2019 programme found no persuasive cold-fusion evidence in its examined conditions. Heat/product accounting and reproducible reference experiments remain challenges. Its externally driven plasma D–D neutrons are a separate result; unachieved loading/untested conditions prevent a universal negative conclusion. Reports unsuccessful electrochemical replication attempts and apparent heat artifacts from input/output measurement errors, changing heat transfer and stored chemical energy, including oxyhydrogen recombination. The authors cannot prove that anomalous heat never exists. These results are scoped to their experiments and do not supply a generally reproducible positive recipe.

principle.assessment: Electroactive bacteria oxidize substrates at the anode while an applied voltage assists cathodic proton reduction to hydrogen. The chemical energy of organics contributes; the device is not electricity generation from water alone.

strength.assessment: The review supports converting waste organics into hydrogen while treating wastewater. Reported examples depend on catalysts, feedstocks and reactor conditions; potential valorisation is not a universal industrial energy or economic gain.

challenge.original_value: Catalyst poisoning and full-system energy accounting
challenge.assessment: Platinum catalyst poisoning and other electrode degradation affect performance. Electricity-only efficiency excludes substrate chemical energy; overall efficiency includes both electrical and substrate inputs. Hydrogen energy above electrical input is not energy creation or a closed positive full-system balance.
